You are no hero - only a sinner crawling out of the Land of the Damned. 

Guided by a Saint who is trapped in a lantern, you push forward by bleeding borrowed Light.

Interact with soul remnants in Hell and unearth memories of your past. 

Borrowed Light is a hack & slash roguelite where story and meta progression are delivered via interactables: enter a map to explore, put the other sinners to rest, and commune with the damned entities of Hell.

Each interactable type triggers a unique dialogue of choices depending on how much of your memory of your earthly deeds you have already unraveled.

The fate of those petrified souls is in your hands, and it is up to you to grant them hope or despair. Ruthlessly harvest their energies, restoring your Light, regaining Memory to become more powerful, and invoking a wide variety of other effects and consequences - or sacrifice a bit of yourself to discover more of their story.

Every interactable features a separate progression path that tells you more about the lost soul behind it, improves the rewards they grant across future playthroughs, and sometimes unravels some of your own deeds back on Earth.

Your Light is your Life: Your borrowed light will be drained by enemy attacks. Squander it all, and you will have to start anew - yet naught is lost, for Hell remembers you: any interactable progression will be retained.

Your Sins are your Skills: Gather memory of your past sins and use it to upgrade each attack in the combo separately for a variety of effects that conditionally buff your damage or deliver other effects - or pick a Memento that will unlock more interaction options.

Your Curses grant Power: Casting burdens you with corruption and forces you to pick Curses that change your appearance - upgrading your future Casts, but accumulating a Light cost

summary:
A pausable 2D real-time strategy game where you command Mars' ships in zero-gravity space battles using realistic Newtonian physics. Outmaneuver Earth’s forces with smart positioning, thruster control, and tactical use of cannons, railguns, and torpedoes.

250 years in the future, Earth and Mars fight over control of the solar system.

 As a junior admiral in the Martian Federal Republic's Space Force, you are responsible to lead your ships to victory over the totalitarian forces of Earth. This is a pauseable real time strategy game, where you must use your spaceships to defeat your enemy.

Unlike some popular (unnamed) franchises, which completely ignore the laws of physics at every turn, Combat In the Void faithfully works with real Newtonian physics giving it a sense of realism. 

At its core, Combat in the Void seeks to be a game that is both realistic to actual physics and also accessible to players who don't want to spend 50 hours learning how to work with a physics simulation. While the controls are straightforward, they still provide interesting challenges and decisions for the player to make.

Torpedoes can fire at long range and deal lots of damage, but can be intercepted by point defense cannons.

Railguns fire at targets within medium range at high velocity. However, they are also expensive to run, so only larger ships have them.

Cannons serve a dual purpose by intercepting enemy torpedoes and also firing on short-range targets.

A successful commander uses these three primary weapon systems effectively to defeat his opponent. Experience space combat that actually feels realistic!

summary:

? About This Game

They said it was just detention. Stay after school. Finish your quizzes. Don’t cause trouble.

But when the lights go out and the halls start whispering, detention becomes something else.

Welcome to Night Detention | 夜の居残り. A paranormal quiz survival set in the haunted school of Akabako. You're a student stuck in after-hours detention. To escape, you must survive three randomized classroom subjects, ace your tests, and dodge whatever's lurking just beyond the classroom.

This case comes from a single thread on the Akabako Community Message Board.

It’s not the only thread. It won’t be the last.

Kōbako

Creepy Quiz Mechanics

Race Against the Bell
After each quiz, navigate school to reach your next classroom before time runs out — or suffer the consequences.

Ghost Encounters
Every wrong answer raises ghost activity. Succeed in handling anomalies or be taken out mid-test.

Multiple Difficulties, Multiple Endings
Choose your punishment level: from Class Pet to Red Room Rules. Your ending changes depending on quiz accuracy, arrival time, and how deep you dig into the school's secrets.

Akabako Message Board Integration
Each run begins as a mysterious forum thread. Your result becomes part of the town’s digital folklore.

? Universe Note

Part of the Kōbako Games
Short games. Long shadows.
Each story is a case pulled from the Akabako Message Board. Rumors, weird things, ghost sightings. Some usernames repeat. Some stories overlap.
The more you play, the more the town remembers you.

You follow the story of Poba, a girl trying to buy a house with her sister within the city of paphollana, after their old one burned down. To achieve this, the two have decided to reopen their father's old cafe at the edge of the city.

As famine, flames and Kaiju ravage the Earth, a small bastion of Humanity holds out on the north pole.  Or at least they did until the Kaiju came for them, too.  Now on a perilous journey, the last of the Scorchwalkers plots it's path from the smoldering ruins of the north, across a fire-torn planet Earth, to the fabled Meadowlands of the south.

Will you recreate our universe or craft brand new ones? What matters is how fast you can reach the target mass.

In this game, you will be aiming to create a universe with the same mass as our own. This can be achieved in many ways. From creating the universe from just 1 element, to creating it out of an equal amount of all the elements.

However, this may seem a bit slow after a while, so Prestiging will give you an opportunity to reset and start over. This time though, you will have a multiplier for your Rate of production for your Sub-Atomic Particles. This will massively speed up your progress.

Your time and score will also be submitted to leaderboards so you can compare who has the current highest mass and who managed to create the universe in the quickest time.

There will also be many achievements along the way. From creating a molecule of water, to recreating the Universe as close as possible.

An explorable digital reconstruction of 924 N 25th Street Apartment 213 in Milwaukee, WI as seen on the early morning hours of July 23, 1991. The environment reflects the residence as it appeared at the time, based on photographs, reports, trial records, and recovered evidence.

In the final minutes of July 22 1991, Milwaukee police were led to 924 N 25th Street Apartment 213 by a man who claimed he was threatened and handcuffed by the resident. Discoveries made during a preliminary search of the residence resulted in an arrest and investigation that would define one of the most difficult chapters in the city’s history. This is a digital reconstruction of that residence as it appeared at the time of the initial investigation, based on photographs, reports, trial records, and recovered evidence. Objects within the space include contextual information drawn from investigative documentation, detailing what was known during the investigation and what was later established. The purpose of this project is documentation, study, and preservation. Viewer discretion is advised.

Intended Audience:

Researchers and students of criminology, forensic science, or criminal history.

True crime enthusiasts interested in detailed, authentic reconstructions.

Anyone seeking a digital preservation of a historically documented crime scene.

Keyboard/Mouse: WASD to navigate, I and O to zoom, spacebar to toggle Forensic View

summary:
You wake up in a locked room The only food is toothpaste. A giant Mouth in the wall eats everything else. Strangers appear. No one trusts anyone. Play quizzes. Win toothpaste! Decorate your room, because you're unsure how long you'll stay here. The Mouth is always hungry.

"They Feed Me Toothpaste" - A Psychological Game

James went to Silverpine Lake with his children to go fishing. He never thought ahead. Just made sure they were seated safely on the old rowboat. As long as they never made it back home... to see what he left behind.

James now wakes up in a sealed, unfamiliar room. On one wall: a gaping hole.

They call it The Mouth.

Feed it, and your remaining time goes down.

Eat its food yourself, and time adds back on. 

The only thing you can eat? Toothpaste.

Soon, others join you in the room.
You’ll compete with them in twisted quizzes. Winners get toothpaste. Losers get nothing. Tensions rise. Trust collapses.

You don't want to stay here with them for too long. You wonder, will time decrease if you feed 'The Mouth' human limbs?

Gameplay

They Feed Me Toothpaste is a narrative-driven walking simulator with a strong focus on psychological horror and character exploration.

As the player, you won’t just observe James’s story. You’ll piece it together.

Each night, you relive key moments from James’s past, experiencing the slow, haunting build-up to his current imprisonment.

There must be a reason why the others got locked up as well, right? From time to time you'll get to relive their past.

Game Features:

Game Time: About 3-4 hours of psychological gameplay.

Quiz Time! Answer the questions correctly or no toothpaste for you!

Explore the horrible acts! You dive into the past of the other characters as they share their horrible stories to you!

Decision-Making: Every decision matters. There are no right or wrong answers... just blame the toothpaste.

Fluoride Toxicity: Eat too much toothpaste, and you might just get a deadly dose of fluoride.

name: Rainbows End
summary:
Robert Gu is a recovering Alzheimer's patient. The world that he remembers was much as we know it today. Now, as he regains his faculties through a cure developed during the years of his near-fatal decline, he discovers that the world has changed and so has his place in it. He was a world-renowned poet. Now he is seventy-five years old, though by a medical miracle he looks much younger, and he’s starting over, for the first time unsure of his poetic gifts. Living with his son’s family, he has no choice but to learn how to cope with a new information age in which the virtual and the real are a seamless continuum, layers of reality built on digital views seen by a single person or millions, depending on your choice. But the consensus reality of the digital world is available only if, like his thirteen-year-old granddaughter Miri, you know how to wear your wireless access—through nodes designed into smart clothes—and to see the digital context—through smart contact lenses.

With knowledge comes risk. When Robert begins to re-train at Fairmont High, learning with other older people what is second nature to Miri and other teens at school, he unwittingly becomes part of a wide-ranging conspiracy to use technology as a tool for world domination.

In a world where every computer chip has Homeland Security built-in, this conspiracy is something that baffles even the most sophisticated security analysts, including Robert’s son and daughter-in law, two top people in the U.S. military. And even Miri, in her attempts to protect her grandfather, may be entangled in the plot.

As Robert becomes more deeply involved in conspiracy, he is shocked to learn of a radical change planned for the UCSD Geisel Library; all the books there, and worldwide, would cease to physically exist. He and his fellow re-trainees feel compelled to join protests against the change. With forces around the world converging on San Diego, both the conspiracy and the protest climax in a spectacular moment as unique and satisfying as it is unexpected.

name: Where Late the Sweet Birds Sang
summary: The spellbinding story of an isolated post-holocaust community determined to preserve itself, through a perilous experiment in cloning. Sweeping, dramatic, rich with humanity, and rigorous in its science, Where Late the Sweet Birds Sang is widely regarded as a high point of both humanistic and hard SF, winning SF's Hugo Award and Locus Award on its first publication.

name: Spin
summary:
One night in October when he was ten years old, Tyler Dupree stood in his back yard and watched the stars go out. They all flared into brilliance at once, then disappeared, replaced by a flat, empty black barrier. He and his best friends, Jason and Diane Lawton, had seen what became known as the Big Blackout. It would shape their lives.

The effect is worldwide. The sun is now a featureless disk--a heat source, rather than an astronomical object. The moon is gone, but tides remain. Not only have the world's artificial satellites fallen out of orbit, their recovered remains are pitted and aged, as though they'd been in space far longer than their known lifespans. As Tyler, Jason, and Diane grow up, space probe reveals a bizarre The barrier is artificial, generated by huge alien artifacts. Time is passing faster outside the barrier than inside--more than a hundred million years per day on Earth. At this rate, the death throes of the sun are only about forty years in our future.

Jason, now a promising young scientist, devotes his life to working against this slow-moving apocalypse. Diane throws herself into hedonism, marrying a sinister cult leader who's forged a new religion out of the fears of the masses.

Earth sends terraforming machines to Mars to let the onrush of time do its work, turning the planet green. Next they send humans...and immediately get back an emissary with thousands of years of stories to tell about the settling of Mars. Then Earth's probes reveal that an identical barrier has appeared around Mars. Jason, desperate, seeds near space with self-replicating machines that will scatter copies of themselves outward from the sun--and report back on what they find.

Life on Earth is about to get much, much stranger.

summary:
You're looking for a new apartment in Amsterdam. Your once-confident search is morphing into panic. Nothing is available. Anything will do. ANYTHING.

Don't Get Your Hopes Up is a short interactive comic about housing shortage and horror in architecture. 

Based on desperate apartment searches undertaken in 2022 and 2024, and drawing from a half decade of conversations about Amsterdam's housing crisis, the game moves between fiction, documentary, and social commentary. 

With disquiet and creeping unease, it dismantles the consoling fictions of abundance, and laments a feeling of home that's always just beyond reach.

Short, emotional, and relatable (unless you're a landlord) 

Playtime: 40-60 minutes. Dive into a week of apartment hunting through the eyes of Krish and Yan, a couple looking to find an apartment in Amsterdam. Classic visual novel gameplay meets sparse, parallax comic book illustrations, with a few narrative and mechanical twists. 

View odd apartments and make tough decisions on renting and overbidding. Experience a moving story about precarity, solidarity, alienation, and the systems that keep us apart. 

A haunting post-punk soundscape 

Immerse yourself in a haunting, propulsive soundscape featuring music by Simon Frank and a special track by Rotterdam band Neighbours Burning Neighbours. 

A uniquely Amsterdam story that is resonant everywhere

"EVERYTHING HAS TO CHANGE, FOR ANYTHING TO STAY THE SAME."

Learn a wayward history of contemporary Amsterdam that is resonant globally. Play through a carefully constructed bricolage of references, ideas, speculations, and social commentary about the housing crisis that attempts to distill fleeting perceptions of an ambient present into coherent yet unsettling images. 

"State-of-the-art maleficence”, with inspirations from Leila Taylor’s Sick Houses, Joshua Comaroff and Ker-Shing Ong’s Horror in Architecture, and Ayşegül Savaş’ The Anthropologists.

Gelato needs your help, cadet! To keep their intergalactic ice-cream truck running, they need to harness the power of the mystical SPACE RUNES that float throughout the cosmos. Luckily, these runes prefer to bind themselves to frozen desserts!

However, these runes are fickle, and their magic only works when they are used to spell words from an arcane language known by some as "English."

Gameplay

The gameplay of WordScoop is simple! You are given a matrix of ice cream scoops, each with a letter on them. Your goal is to find words by connecting adjacent scoops! You can go in any direction you want, but they have to be contiguous. When the word is ready, click again on the last scoop to submit it.

If you spell longer words, bonus sprinkles will appear on existing scoops! Submitting a word with these will apply a multiplier to the points you earn from it.

Be careful, however! Relying too much on short words will cause more VOID scoops to spawn. These greedy creatures love eating both RUNES and ice cream, so you can bet that they're trouble! They appear at the top of the screen and gradually eat their way down, so make sure they don't hit the bottom. Otherwise, it's game over.

summary:
Ramshackle is a multiplayer sandbox game where you design a combat vehicle, or "Vessel", out of destructible parts and armor, and put it to the test against other player-driven and AI Vessels. Share designs with other players on your server or license it out to the AI and encounter it in battle!

Ramshackle is a twist on the vehicular build-and-combat genre. Instead of piecing together blocks, you construct vehicles (referred to as "vessels" in-game) with point-placed struts and armor plates as the core structure. Functional modules like wheels, tracks, and weapons integrate into this framework, but they only work when powered by engines, transmission lines, and ammunition. Combat then plays out with simulated ballistics: angled armor can deflect rounds, while a well-placed shot into an ammo rack can tear a vehicle apart from the inside.

Features

Designer

- Construct your vessel's structure using an advanced vertex-based armor editor.

- Plan your vessel around internal modules. Get five car engines and put them together!

Single-player, Multiplayer

- Battle on a variety of terrains across different "Tech" levels, representing eras of military vehicle development.

- Engage designs made by other players, operated by those players, or AI opponents.

Unique Roles

- A vessel's tradeoffs between armor, firepower, mobility, and utility will determine its success in battle. Designs range from heavily-armored brawlers to paper-thin scouts, and everything in between.

summary:
This game is an innovative twist on classic snake - style games

This game is an innovative twist on classic snake - style games, building its core gameplay around a minimalist 2D cartoon aesthetic. Set against a bright green background, a tiger - shaped snake head leads a body made of red circular segments. Players must dodge black stone obstacles while devouring bright red apples to score points and lengthen the snake.

Core Mechanics & Innovations

It inherits the classic snake loop of “eat → grow → escalate in difficulty”, but redefines the challenge with static black stones. The snake must avoid not only self - collision, but also navigate around rocks—even predicting pathing as its body grows. Each apple eaten boosts the score by 1 and extends the snake; as length increases, demands for precision and spatial strategy skyrocket. Players balance “greedy growth” against “survival,” with reflexes and decision - making tested relentlessly.

Visuals & Experience

The interface is stripped - down: a “Score” at the top tracks progress, and an “Exit” button in the top - right enables quick exits, perfect for short play sessions. Visual design is playful: the tiger - headed snake adds charm, apples stand out clearly, and black stones signal danger unambiguously. The pace ramps up with the snake’s length—starting as relaxed apple - collecting, then devolving into frantic maneuvers to avoid tangling in its own body or hitting obstacles. This creates a satisfying “easy to start, hard to master” thrill.

Controls

Move Up = W

Move Down = S

Move Left = A

Move Right = D

Skaldsong is a multiplayer RPG platform that combines the deep mechanics of classic CRPGs with the narrative freedom of tabletop role-playing. Here, the story is not pre-written. It's generated live, guided either by a human Game Master using our toolset, or by an advanced generative AI that acts as your Game Master.

There is daily free AI Usage for everyone!

Stuck as a forever DM? Lacking friends but want to play a TTRPG? Have friends but nobody wants to be the one to run the game? Just want to see what AI can do?

Then this game is for you.

A True RPG Engine

Skaldsong is not another hastily thrown together AI chatbot. It is a complete game engine with robust, underlying systems that feel like a modern evolution of classic MUDs (Multi-User Dungeons). The AI's role is not to solely run the game, but to create content for it.

You are not limited to pure adventure games, using custom Game Rules, you can play all sorts of games- Slice of Life school romance? The management of a mercenary company? Fight in the gladiator pits? Interstellar Empire management? With the right ruleset, the AI can smoothly run about any game you can define.

When the AI responds to your actions, its narrative is embedded with special . Our custom parser reads these tags and translates them into mechanical changes within the game state. If the AI describes you finding a sword, a tag mechanically adds that sword to your inventory. This system ensures that the story and the game mechanics are always perfectly in sync.

While the interaction is text-based, the world is fully visualized. You are not just reading text; you are interacting with graphical character sheets, inventory windows, a world map, quest logs, and more.

Set sail across a shifting sea in this colorful pixel-art adventure. Battle enemy ships, meet goofy islanders, collect magical eggs and awaken the kraken. A compact, handcrafted, free-to-play game.

Set sail into the unknown in Atollo, a vibrant, pixel-art sea adventure where every journey is unique. Explore a shifting archipelago, meet goofy island dwellers, and battle rival ships to collect five magical eggs - your only key to awakening the kraken at the heart of the map.

FEATURES

?️ Ever-changing map
Explore a procedurally generated archipelago - no two voyages are the same.

? Fast-paced naval combat
Face off against enemy ships in tight, tactical battles on the open sea.

? Bizarre island encounters
Visit 5 random islands per run and meet one of 24 whimsical characters - from moons with sunglasses to haunted coffee pots.

? The egg hunt begins
Earn magical eggs from the islanders. Collect all five to summon your final challenge.

? Face the kraken
Unlock the center of the map and confront a colossal sea beast in a thrilling endgame battle.

? Progress artwork
After each run, view a unique scene featuring the characters you’ve met - and silhouettes for those yet to be found.

A GAME MADE WITH PICO-8

Atollo is a standalone desktop release built entirely in Pico-8, a fantasy console for tiny retro games. Development on Pico-8 is a celebration of creative constraints, compact code, and playful design - and it’s free to play.

ABOUT THE DEVELOPER

Hello ! I'm Alberto and I'm a solo developer with a passion for expressive games :)) Atollo was created from start to finish by me, from the design and code to the art and audio, as a personal challenge and a way to grow as a game maker.

I’m releasing Atollo for free with the goal of sharing something fun, goofy and replayable, while building a portfolio that can help me take the next step into the game development industry.

If you enjoyed the game or have any feedback, I’d love to hear from you! :))

summary:
A different kind of solitaire. More difficult, more strategic.

A different kind of solitaire.

Accordion Solitaire is a more difficult, more strategic variation of solitaire. Starting with a shuffled deck, you will draw cards and make decisions about how to stack them based on matching ranks and suits. But there are strict rules about when cards can be stacked:

When a stack is adjacent to a matching rank or suit.

When a stack is separated from a matching rank or suit by exactly two other stacks.

The goal of the game is to begin with one deck of cards, and end up with one stack of cards. It will be trickier than you might think!

Features

Multiple Rulesets

Accordion Solitaire features 3 rulesets that change the way the game is played:

Strict

Draw one card at a time, and all possible moves must be made before drawing again.

Relaxed

Draw one card at a time, but you can continue to draw without making all possible moves if you choose.

Free

Draw the entire deck at once and play with full knowledge.

Accessibility

Accordion Solitaire comes with some accessibility features that make it possible for all to play.

Possible move hints

When holding a stack, possible moves will be highlighted to make it easier to understand your options. Defaults to On.

Auto draw

Automatically draw cards until there is a possible move (only applicable when using Strict or Relaxed rules) so you don't have to click the deck manually as often. Defaults to On.

Reduced motion

By default stacks shake when they have possible moves to make it easier to understand your options. If the shaking is distracting or overwhelming, you can force all stacks to stay still. Defaults to Off.

High contrast

Places a color filter over each suit to make it easier to understand when stacks have matching suits. Defaults to Off.

Music & Sound

Fully adjustable Music and Sound sliders allow you to modify volume in-game. Music and Sound can also be enabled or disabled. Defaults to enable Music and Sound

summary:

If only I could see you once again...

Story

Akira’s world shattered the moment he saw his girlfriend Yuki’s lifeless body on the pavement after a horrific car crash. Weeks later, he joins his professor, Akane, on a trip to investigate the legendary Kagetsu Mansion—a site tied to the Amayorome Myth of a god imprisoned and a land condemned.

Upon reaching the mansion, Akira discovers it is more than a ruin. In his sleep, he is transported to a version of the estate that is still thriving. There, he meets the mysterious hostess Sayuri, her servant Mizuki, and her daughter Momiji—and is reunited with Yuki. However, Akira soon learns this sanctuary hides an evil corrupting his mind. Psychological Romance: Navigate Akira’s deep-seated longing for his lost love. Experience intimate and emotional moments that blur the line between a beautiful dream and a predatory trap.

Cosmic Horror: Witness a unique fusion of Lovecraftian dread and Japanese folklore.

summary:
Hackers have encrypted your data and it's your job to hack them back.  Explore a procedurally generated network using an arsenal of terminal commands to find the encryption key.

In HACK.BAK, the group F.I.S.H (Frivolous Information Sealing Hackers) have encrypted your precious data.  They've left you the tools you need to find the key, but they're spread across a network of servers, routers, and other devices.  Your job is to find the commands, traverse the network, and unlock your data.

Key Features

Terminal-based Gameplay: Enter commands like you would in a linux terminal or windows command prompt.  Supports tab-completion and command history.

Procedurally Generated: No two games are exactly alike.  The order you'll find the commands and the layout of the network will change with each new game.

Network Size Options: Choose from a small, medium, or large game.  The network map doubles in size with each increase.

Decryption Puzzle: Solve a bitmask puzzle to decrypt commands, but if puzzles aren't your thing, feel free to turn it off in the options.

Flexible Control Options: The game is fully controllable using just the keyboard, but that doesn't mean you have to.  The game has controller support (native Xbox controller or Steam Input) as well as mouse support (with limited keyboard requirement).  

All actions can be performed using the context menu via menu-key (or shift+F10), controller "Context Menu" binding, or mouse right-click.

Use your mouse, numpad directional, or controller joystick to navigate the network.

Welcome to "The Authority," the cosmic organization responsible for managing the life-death cycle of... everything.
You are a reaper - technically an employee - tasked with serving Final Notices to immortal entities who refuse to retire on schedule.

As with most jobs, you're expected to learn on the job, break a few things, and file the relevant forms afterward.

Final Notice is a dense, puzzle-like solo deckbuilder where you are encouraged - professionally obligated, even - to lose. Losing reveals weaknesses. Weaknesses become strategies. Strategies become victories you can brag about in the break room.

If you're hoping to win your first fight, you're in the wrong department.

Experimenting with 110+ cards designed to synergize, contradict each other, and occasionally betray you.

Managing mortis, a soul-derived resource that Health & Safety insists is "safe enough" to use unsupervised.

Building and rebuilding decks after each inevitable workplace accident.

Battling procedurally generated bosses built from adjective-domain combinations.

Tracking status effects like Banished, Fogged, and Entombed - all of which are definitely covered under your contract. Maybe.

Revising your strategy because your starter deck is about as effective as a stapler against a hurricane.

THE INTENDED LOOP (PLEASE READ - HR INSISTS):

Attempt a boss fight.

Lose. (This is normal. Please stop filing incident reports.)

Return to the deckbuilder.

Rethink your life choices.

Discover a synergy you didn't notice before.

Beat the boss.

Hit a harder boss.

Restart at Step 2 until you clock out or management intervenes.

If you enjoy figuring things out yourself, welcome aboard.
If you prefer a guided tour and guaranteed wins, HR recommends transferring to another department.

summary:
A veteran hitman, bored with routine assignments, alters their perception with a mind-bending drug, shifting to a stripped-down reality, where they perceive only sounds as light as they eliminate their targets as fast as possible to earn more money.

Summary

W|RE is a short fast-paced, first-person shooter where you play as a veteran hitman—tired of routine contracts—who takes a mind-altering drug that radically changes how he perceives the world. In this altered state, sound becomes light: every gunshot, footstep, or musical beat sends out colorful waves that briefly illuminate the environment in glowing outlines.

Your mission is simple: reach the target location and eliminate your enemies as fast and precisely as possible. The faster you are, the more money you earn. If you're not satisfied with your performance, try again—perfect your rhythm, and climb the highscore ladder.

Goal

The goal is to clear all rooms in a level as quickly and efficiently as possible while maximizing your score. Your final score is affected by several factors, including clear time, headshot count, hits and accuracy. The better you perform, the more your employer is willing to pay - and the higher you climb on the leaderboard.

Setting

The world of W|RE is inspired by the cyberpunk aesthetic: dark, industrial environments lit by vibrant color and driven by pulsing music. A short comic-style cutscene introduces each run, explaining your mission and setting the tone. Speakers placed throughout the world reinforce the rhythm, making every level feel like a playable beat-driven hallucination where your perception is as much a weapon as your gun.

 Nine years ago, the celebrated neurologist Dr. Alistair Blackwood vanished from his own institution, the Blackwood Sanatorium. summary:
Wander through a shifting, atmospheric home that responds to your presence. Break the cycle, uncover subtle meanings, or simply enjoy a quiet, unsettling psychological experience.

A Space Shaped by What You Carry

The Quiet Weight is a restrained, symbolic horror experience about the cycles we return to when processing our deepest pains. Rooms shift. Paths close. New ones open only when you're ready to face what's waiting. You're not escaping a place — you're moving through something you've been avoiding.

Atmospheric Horror Through Subtle Change

The world reacts quietly to your presence. A vent opens that wasn't open before. A door strains, as if holding something back. A hallway feels narrower than before. Something responds to every step you take — shaped by what still hurts, and what you're not ready to see.

Move Carefully Through What Remains

Sound matters. Stillness matters. Attention matters. You'll navigate:

Shifting rooms shaped by memory.

Fragile spaces that hold what you've left untouched.

Moments of pressure pressing through the walls.

A quiet presence built from the parts of yourself you've tried not to feel.

Not every part of you is ready at the same time — and the house reflects that.

Cycles That Change When You Do

Each loop reveals something new — not because the world is random, but because you are different each time you return. You're not retracing someone else's steps. You're retracing your own. And when you're ready, the house will lead you back to the moment you've been carrying.

-----------------------------------------

Failing is Guaranteed

The two entities the HEC and the PPU (Pilakarrian Planetary Union) would begin trying to establish economic trade, but a mistranslation led to a HEC trade caravan being attacked by the PPU. This would set off a war between the two nations. The PPU were quick to launch their assault on the desert world of Mars, they would capture the Martian capital of New Olympus within weeks. The HEC Generals are scrambling as the PPU are making their preparations to attack the HEC Capitol of Earth. 

Take command of the human defenses in a traditional Tower Defense style game. Then repel the invading forces by creating your counter assaults to invade their territory, use military strategy to determine which towers will be best suited for the defenses. Bring home glory for the HEC. Explore a linear story to defend Earth and her colonies and be remembered as a hero, you will work alongside several generals who will aid your journey towards solving this conflict.

Flood Descendance is a unique spin on the delverlike genre. Race against a relentless flood as you work with up to 5 other players to escape a flooded, abandoned facility. Every floor is a race against a flood that never waits.

DESCEND OR DROWN

Enter floors with one key objective: descend to the next. Work fast and smart to activate buttons, twist valves, fuel generators and more, all while outrunning the flood to make it to the escape elevator, without drowning.

PARKOUR YOUR WAY TO SAFETY

Master agility to stay one step ahead. Jump and climb your way through tower sections where the wrong step can leave you falling into a pit of molten lava.

SURVIVE THE FLOOD

Whether it be water, acid or lava, the flood does not stop. Swim through flooded sections while watching your (limited) oxygen.

GO DEEPER WITH STRATEGY

Spend your XP on permanent, team-wide upgrades such as increased oxygen and faster movement while floors get progressively harder the deeper you descend.

WORK TOGETHER (or not...)

Success is easier with teamwork, but not everyone's fit to be a hero. Split up to cover more ground, work together on teamwork-required puzzles, revive drowned teammates, or leave them behind if it means reaching the elevator yourself. Just remember: it's to push.

DISCOVER THE STORY OR DESCEND DEEPER

Experience a handcrafted campaign to uncover Flodtech's secrets and the horrors left behind by those who used to work there, or test your limits by descending as deep as possible through procedurally generated floors.*

Arcade mode drops you into the garage for a pure score chase. Leaks escalate the longer you survive, and every clean catch beats letting water hit the floor. Dump into the drain to stay alive, stack trick-shot multipliers, and push your high score.

Defend the House turns it into a four room run. Start in the bedroom, then push through the bathroom, kitchen and living room in order. Each room has a fixed leak quota. Survive long enough for that many leaks to fully finish instead of racing the drain. When the quota is met the door unlocks and you move to the next room.

Floor water carries across the whole run. When you step into a new room the current floor water is cut in half since the same water is now spread over more of the house, but it never fully resets. If the water line reaches your head height in any room the run is over.

Between key levels you visit the wizard shopkeeper. Pick one boon from a small set of random options. Slow down leak spawns, reduce how many leaks can be active, move faster, throw farther or bring a safety tool that cuts the water bar or saves you once from a drowning spike. Boons last for that run and follow you between rooms. New runs start clean.

If you want a softer version you can flip on Chill Vibes. Floor water caps at a safer level and slowly drains back down so you can practice routes, containers and throws without losing the whole run as quickly.

Few words from the devs: 

“For inspirations we looked towards the older days. In terms of aesthetics we wanted to accommodate the simplicity of the Space Race US and Soviet propaganda poster. “Once we observed people playing early vaguely-balanced version of Master Lander, we knew that unforgiving skill-based challenge is the way to go. And frankly, only half of our team was able to beat the game by the time of release.” - Adam Wołoszczuk, co-designer

summary:
A simple interactive, touch-screen supported, game targeted to younger children to help build up early motor and logic skills

Children's Sandbox is a very simple game that was created by parents for their children, and it feels only fair to release this game to others who may want something simple to help children with fine motor and logic skills.

Children's Sandbox is made up of 9 different simple games for children to play. These games help with things as simple as reaction speed, dragging and dropping capabilities, correlation with colors and shapes, memorization, and other skills. Of course, to do this, we need simple games that children will enjoy and not feel "tested" with. Therefore, each of these mini games on their own feel like simple things that children can enjoy on their own without realizing they're building up on skills that may help them early on.

Depending on your child's place with milestones and other various natural factors, this game can probably be played and enjoyed from age 2 to 4. Of course, bare in mind screen time at these young ages - please keep it to a minimum!

The game is made up of three difficulties. Easy tends to slow games down or lower the number of requirements to "meet a goal", where as medium and hard will increase these speeds or number requirements. It's recommended to start on easy, see how your child does, and then change the difficulty to what feels right! Each game may have to be tweaked to different difficulties, depending on where your child is with the respective skill.

About:

After four years navigating the bureaucracy of the legal system first has as a superior court clerk, I transformed my firsthand knowledge into the satirical indie game Attorney Disbarment Adventure, now available on Steam. It's a darkly comedic legal sim where players aim not to uphold the law, but to spectacularly fail within it. The game blends moral ambiguity, Kafkaesque dilemmas, and a branching narrative to challenge the traditional justice-fueled power fantasy.

My creative path began in storytelling and modding, but now I focus on original games that explore real-world systems through interactive fiction and dark humor. I believe games should do more than entertain—they should question authority, dissect ideology, and leave players reflecting long after the credits roll. I build the kinds of worlds that demand ethical curiosity, where "winning" might mean losing your soul, and every playthrough rewrites your sense of right and wrong.

About the Game

Burn your law career on purpose in Ambicity, an overstressed legal ecosystem where “success” just prolongs your misery. As a scorched-out public defender, you juggle frantic legal minigames, contradictory ethics boards, and resilience systems that keep trying to rehabilitate you. Collapse six disbarment archetypes—Incompetent, Corrupt, Burnout, Negligent, Unethical, Tragic—by failing with precision instead of button-mashing every objective into oblivion.

EXAMPLE PLAYSTYLES:

Hire anybody you can, don't be picky about who you fight, fall back while vulnerable, and get your combat-related skills nice and high through use.

Each playthrough ends on defeat while vulnerable, or at the retirement deadline. Reaching retirement is a victory, but you can beat your personal best score even if you don't.

Open world travel as a mercenary band.

A full system of terrain properties and weather events.

Use-it-to-improve-it skills.

Goal

The goal of Bank is to collect all the money bags in each level. Only then does the key activate. Then you can collect the key and complete the level.

- This is money. You need this because there's an economic recession.

- This is the key.  If it's grey then there's still money you need to get.  But if it's gold then you can touch it to end the level.

- This is a bomb.

Four eras. One destiny.

Zenogaias is a sweeping, turn-based JRPG that spans the ages from 8-bit Medieval Fantasy to HD Sci-Fi/Fantasy fusion across four full-length Episodes, each inspired by a different era of gaming while delivering on its classic roots throughout. 

Linked together by a powerful, epic narrative, each Episode evolves in tone, visuals, mechanics, and music to reflect the growth of the genre itself while exploring themes of fate, identity, and the unbreakable bonds forged across generations.

(8-bit | Fantasy)

Dame Alyria, a battle-hardened knight and mother, is given a nigh on insurmountable task with uncovering its source before humanity becomes extinct. Journey across a land of danger and secrets in a tale that echoes the classic roots from JRPGs of yesteryear.

EPISODE II — The Watcher & The Deliverer

(16-bit | Fantasy)
Dame Captain Rei leads an elite airship squadron during a time of political upheaval. Betrayed during the mission and stranded in enemy territory, she uncovers a truth that challenges everything she had ever known. Unravel a growing conspiracy across the snowy northern regions in this war story where all is not as it seems. 

EPISODE III — The Beginning and the End

(PSX-inspired | Sci-Fi)
In the far future, a galactic war looms over the discovery of a powerful energy source, the Razael Particle. Realtime physics

We are making a game with accurate physics. As such we implemented a realtime buoyancy system based on weight and submerged volume. The ship density and center of mass is displayed in editor, allowing to fine tune your ship and even make submarines using ballasts !

summary:
A unique and casual chess experience with new rules and luck-based mechanics which requires fresh strategies, tactics, and ingenuity to conquer.

Chess of Fortune is a unique variant of the game of chess. It is a simple game based on luck and strategy. 

The game uses standard chess pieces and is played on half of a standard chess board. The rules for moving and capturing pieces have been completely revamped and the game incorporates an element of randomness when bringing each piece into play. It has simple rules and moves which are less complex than that of generic chess, and are thus easier to pick up and master. 

Chess of Fortune is perfect for players who are looking to engage in quicker and more casual game than generic chess while honing their strategic thinking skills. Master these new rules and develop fresh strategies to manage the fickleness of luck in order to triumph over your opponents.

Game Features

Single player vs AI mode

Local multiplayer mode for 2 players.

Tutorial on how to play the game.

Color customization options for game pieces.

Basic scoring and level progression system.

Game Rules

General gameplay: Each player starts with a standard set of chess pieces. However the chess pieces are hidden in anonymous boxes that are randomly assigned throughout the board at the beginning of the game. The players then take alternate turns playing. On each of their turn, a player may either open a box to free up a piece or move any of their previously freed pieces. A "Score" is another way of saying "20", so "Two Score" means "40".

A Fantasy Adventure

At the edge of a kingdom guided by magic and ruled by technology lies a crystal holding immense power. Coming into this world as a vat-grown supersoldier, you know nothing except that you have been told that this crystal is dangerous and must be destroyed. Thus you embark on your adventure to save the kingdom.

Overview

Tsujigiri is a 2D Roguelike Platformer, inspired by titles like Spelunky, Super Smash Brothers, and Hollow Knight. Adventure through procedurally-generated levels to progress, and fight enemies and collect loot as you go. Every encounter you win makes you stronger, and exploration is rewarded with money and items. Fight bosses throughout the levels that test your mettle. Engaging Combat

The combat system is simple to pick up, yet as you become more experienced it has much to master. There is a lot of combat in this game, and it is the main aspect of your character that you upgrade. Based on the direction you hold and whether you are grounded or airborne, you can perform different attacks. You start each run with simple attacks, but you can perform more complex actions as you upgrade your moveset.

Two Movesets

Switch between body form and ball form anytime, each with a unique moveset. Overcome challenges by using the tools of each based on the situation. The body form is easier to control and equipped with a sword for combat for reach and crowd control, while the ball form is more agile and can body bash in combat for mobility and single-target damage.

summary:
A fast, unforgiving roguelite where short, procedural mazes chain into long, high-stakes runs. Move precisely, spend gems wisely, and escape... or start over.

Exit Plan b is a fast, unforgiving roguelite arcade game where each run drops you into a procedurally generated maze that will not wait for you.

Each level throws you into a new maze, unique to your run. Once you step inside, you must adapt and move with purpose. Mistakes matter. Your objective is simple: collect enough points to spawn the exit and escape. Surviving long enough to do that is the real challenge.

Procedurally Generated Levels

Fast, Focused Stages

Single levels are quick to complete, chaining together into longer, high-stakes runs.

Risk–Reward Skill System

Powerful abilities cost gems earned during the run. Spend aggressively or save for survival. Every choice matters.

Pure Arcade Flow

Tight movement, fast pacing, and instant restarts keep the focus on skill and mastery.

Escalating Difficulty

Pressure builds as runs go deeper, rewarding precision, learning, and smart decision-making.

summary:
An RPG Maker MZ game done in the style of a 1980s NES RPG, with a NES-styled (but not NES authentic) soundtrack.

This game is free to download, with the option to support me by purchasing the OST and/or the strategy guide.  You are welcome to download it for free and come back later to buy an extra if you decide to.  No ads, no data collection, just free with the option of buying something, if you decide you liked it enough to support me!

I wanted to have my own music in a game, so decided to make my own game.  This is the full version of a prologue/demo I released in early 2025. It was made in RPG Maker MZ.

Essentially, this is a 1980s NES styled RPG, with some modern quality of life to make it more accessible. It does still have some 1980s NES RPG RNG that will cause game overs at times, as part of the design. It has turn-based combat, challenging boss encounters (where you can get RNG screwed just like the old days!), and it has been designed to have a minimal amount of grinding (maybe 20 minutes total intentional grinding on the 2nd fastest game speed). You control a party of four with different skillsets, enemies have weaknesses you can exploit for max damage, some enemies will even reflect your spells back at you!

The soundtrack uses the free NES VST plugin for instruments, so it is authentic to NES in that sense. However, it uses a seperate plugin for vibrato to give it a unique sound - this plugin is not NES authentic. Also, while the visual art pack I bought was NES authentic, I occasionally made changes that were not NES authentic because I didn't like the limitations it sometimes imposed (ie. map sprite coloring being a mismatch with combat sprite coloring). The drums were made using Tweakbench Toad, which is NES authentic. While I did want the game to be like NES, ultimately I wanted to try doing something a little different to set it apart.

summary:
Math and Guns is a top-down shooter where solving math problems is used to reload your guns. Play as a dubiously colored bounty hunter as you fight against generic monsters with fully automatic arithmetic, or just solve math problems and be boring, that's also an option.

You are Leifren Von Green, a powerful bounty hunter with a magical green hat granting unlimited ammunition for any weapon, with the condition that you solve some math problems for it, of course. You'll be fighting off hordes of zombies, skeletons, and other generic monsters as a one man army and your next target is an arrogant, power-hungry necromancer that desires nothing less than the death of all things green. 

Usage of this game as an educational tool

        There is no intent to mask that there are in fact guns in this game. Despite mental math being a core part of this game it is not intended for instructional use within normal school environments. It is up to the discretion of those purchasing to decide how to use it. With all of that said, for those who desire to freshen up their mental math skills, this game is a fantastic way of doing so. It includes options for customizing the math problems presented to players, so now those who would like to quickly know what 67 squared is have easy access to a game built to expand their mental math capabilities.

summary:
Rail Nomads is a top-down, co-op extraction shooter. Your base is a mobile, armored train. Battle mutants, rebels, and rival players in unique raids through a post-apocalyptic world. Risk it all for the reward!

In Rail Nomads, you are an elite survivor in a post-apocalyptic wasteland where the key to survival is your unique base of operations: a fully customizable, armored train. This game merges the intense co-op of Helldivers with the high-stakes, gear-loss tension of Escape from Tarkov, all from a unique top-down tactical perspective.

The Addictive Risk & Reward Loop

The core gameplay is an addictive cycle of risk and reward. Accept dynamic contracts from a mission board that lead you on dangerous expeditions across vast sectors of an interconnected world. Each sector is a persistent map where the content (enemies, loot, objectives) is pseudo-procedural, ensuring no two raids are ever the same and keeping exploration fresh and surprising.

The Triple Threat: Unpredictable PvEvP

Survival depends on your tactical skill, resource management, and—crucially—squad cooperation. Face a constant triple threat: hordes of aggressive mutants (PvE), hostile factions of human raiders (PvE), and the most unpredictable menace of all: opportunistic rival players competing for the same resources (PvP). The fear of losing your uninsured gear is what drives every high-stakes decision you make.

Your Train: The Heart of Your Operations

Your train is more than a base; it's your moving home and a visible trophy of your progress. Explore its various cars, each with a vital function for your survival and expansion:

Locomotive: Chart your course and accept missions on the world map.

Armory Car: Modify and customize your weapons with an immersive 3D interface.

Workshop Car: Craft consumables (medkits, grenades), repair damaged gear, and build new weapons and armor from rare blueprints.

Medical Car: Heal persistent injuries from your raids and create stimulants for temporary buffs

summary:
Toonish: a game about exploration, exploitation, and money.

Toonish is a game about exploration, exploitation, and money set in an alternate universe with hostile creatures, competing companies, a̶n̶d̶ ̶a̶n̶c̶i̶e̶n̶t̶ ̶g̶o̶d̶s̶ ̶b̶e̶y̶o̶n̶d̶ ̶c̶o̶m̶p̶r̶e̶h̶e̶n̶s̶i̶o̶n̶.̶

You play as a toon named Edward Scotts, who after moving out of his city house decides to purchase a boat ticket to a small island of the cost of the Pacific ocean, leaving him with only a pickaxe, an axe, a shovel, and $100 to his name.

In order to make money, you will have to exploit local supply chains and industrialize everything in order to make enough to not just thrive, but to be well off and never have to work a day in your life ever again.

There are many ways to make money in the world of Toonish, whether it be simplistic and small-scale, like farming or hunting, or somthing that can be industrialized and perfected to no end, such as a large-scale mining or construction industry, or even becoming the mayor of a town and taxing your citizens.

However, there are certain prominent figures who will not like the exploration you are doing, and will stop at no costs to not only end your company, industry, and whatever you own, but you yourself as well.

Build, survive, thrive, and fight against the odds in a world that gets more nonsensical the longer you explore it; all in Toonish.

summary:
Set in a medieval Europe-inspired world, you begin with a single city and a handful of territories on a vast hex-based map. Expand your domain, conquer new lands and lead your house and empire to glory in a time-based Massively Multiplayer setting.

NobleFront is a time-based Massive Multiplayer Strategy game where you begin with a single city on a vast, hex-based world map and rise to power by expanding your lands and outmaneuvering rival players.

As the head of your House, you govern a living society composed of distinct population classes, each with a vital role. 

Farmers cultivate fields and provide the food that sustains your realm.

Laborers form the backbone of manual work, employed in logging camps, construction projects, and urban workshops under the supervision of artisans.

Miners extract essential raw materials such as clay and iron, important for building materials and weapon making.

Artisans transform raw materials into refined goods, producing household goods, weapons, building materials, and luxury items required by both the economy and the elites.

Bureaucrats oversee and regulate all population classes, ensuring efficient employment, production as well as consumption.

Officers lead and organize your armies, directly affecting military effectiveness and battlefield performance.

Merchants form the backbone of trade. They are vital for the transport and exchange of goods between cities and players.

Lastly, the Upper Class represents nobles and wealthy elites, eagerly waiting to consume refined goods in exchange for gold which is essential for funding your armies.

Production in NobleFront is driven by a network of medieval buildings constructed within individual territories, each tied directly to your population. Every production building employs specific population classes and converts labor into value, either by extracting raw materials or by transforming them into refined goods.

 Resources are produced locally and do not move automatically.

summary:
Search dumpsters for hidden treasures in this realistic first-person simulation. Load heavy furniture onto your truck, separate materials, and sell to scrap dealers. Start with nothing and build your urban scavenging empire.

Welcome to the world of urban treasure hunting. 

Every dumpster tells a story. That old lamp might be worthless junk  or a vintage collector's item worth hundreds. In Dumpster Diving Simulator, experience the thrill of discovery that real dumpster divers know all too well. 

SEARCH AND DISCOVER Explore realistic urban environments filled with dumpsters waiting to be searched. Each container holds procedurally generated items  from common recyclables to rare vintage finds. Examine everything carefully. Condition matters when it comes to value. 

LOAD AND HAUL Found a refrigerator or a couch? Use physics-based mechanics to lift, carry, and load heavy furniture onto your truck. Master the art of efficient stacking to maximize each haul. 

SELL AND PROFIT Build relationships with scrap dealers who pay based on material and weight. Separate metals, plastics, electronics, and more. Learn the market, find the best buyers, and watch your profits grow.

- Physics-based heavy item carrying and truck loading 
- Dynamic loot system with varying item conditions and values 
- Multiple scrap dealers with different specialties - Upgradeable truck and equipment 
- Relaxing, open-world exploration 
- Economy system inspired by real scrap trading

summary:
Glitch and Glory: Tales of Honeywood is a parody RPG where you, an adventurer, tackle absurd quests in a satirical MMORPG world. Save sheep, negotiate with ghosts, and avoid fines. Sarcastic dialogue, impactful choices, and retro graphics await!

About This Game

Glitch and Glory: Tales of Honeywood is a hilarious parody of classic MMORPGs, inspired by the humor of Epic NPC Man from Viva La Dirt League and the absurdity of classic fantasy. Dive into the ridiculous world of Honeywood, where you, a hapless adventurer, tackle absurd quests, battle NPC bureaucracy, and try not to mess everything up. Save sheep, fight spiders (or puppies?), negotiate with ghosts, and dodge fines from the Order of Paladins of Alderkeep. Expect sarcastic dialogue, unexpected twists, and a ton of nods to MMO culture.

Venture into the village of Honeywood, where every resident—from garlic farmer Greg to pompous wizard Baradun—is ready to throw a bizarre task your way. Read (or skip) instructions, choose between an axe or a broom, and try not to become the town’s laughingstock. Can you survive this chaotic world where even a chicken can get you in trouble with the whole village?

Key Features:

MMORPG Parody: Satire on quests, NPCs, and gaming clichés packed with humor.

Choices with Consequences: Your decisions impact reputation and outcomes.

Absurd Characters: Meet the bureaucratic Quartermaster, philosophical gravediggers, and enigmatic Priestess.

In-Game Achievements: Earn rewards for persistence (or sheer stupidity).

Retro Style: Classic pixel art and dialogue in the spirit of RPG Maker MZ.

References and Easter Eggs: Nods to famous fantasy novels, MMORPGs, and other iconic games and worlds.

If you’re ready to laugh at yourself and the absurdity of MMORPGs, Glitch and Glory is your ticket to an absurd adventure!

In this wave-based flight action game, military airships threaten the peace above the clouds. Only the bird shepherd Mona has the tools to lead thousands of sharp-beaked birds into battle against the invaders to shred their balloons and send them back to the surface.

Aerial Combat Without Weapons

Beakstorm is a wave-based flight action game, in which you play as Mona, a bird shepherd who needs to defend her home above the clouds against waves of invading industrial airships. Her glider has no weapons installed, instead she has massive quantities of bird pheromone at her disposal, which she can use to direct flocks of sharp-beaked birds into the balloons of the enemy.

Lead Birds Into Battle

Birds are the only way to deal damage to enemies, so you will need to use all tools at your disposal to guide them towards your targets. Pheromone can be dispensed either directly from Mona's glider, or it can be shot out using a variety of unlockable projectiles, all of which have unique effects on the birds around them.

Face The Behemoths From Below

The surface has been taken over by ravenous industry and greedy corporations. They have started sending a variety of airships to now conquer the skies, and you will need to fend them off!

Follow Mona's resistance in the Campaign, as she not only defends against the airships, but starts to attack their facilities and undermines their coal production. Play through 10 various missions – each 10 to 15 minutes long –, which see you both defeating waves off enemies and completing other objectives, such as destroying enemy facilities on mountain tops and defending your village against attackers. Missions are graded by your performance and time, so mastery over your glider is key to chasing gold ranks! 

Alternatively, Arcade Mode pits you against unending waves of enemies with ever increasing difficulty. Between waves, choose between restoring health and changing your projectile type, as you are limited to only one in this mode. Mast

When the weapon is ready, the final confrontation begins. You’ll have only one chance. And one shot.

Short sessions, maximum tension:

Exit Denied is designed for compact play sessions – perfect for quick adrenaline rushes or spontaneous horror rounds in between.

Developer’s Note: “Exit Denied” is my first released game. I’m using this project to gain experience in game development.

Lead a squad of tiny heroes in a fast-paced tactical RPG where every move is on the clock. Build your own team, outwit crafty enemies, and craft powerful builds in endlessly replayable roguelike runs.

Command your squad of pint-sized heroes in a fast-paced tactical RPG where timing is everything. In Mini Scouts, every hero and enemy acts on their own timer — manipulate the action queue, outsmart your foes, and build unstoppable synergies in ever-changing roguelike runs.

Key Features

Asynchronous Action Queue Combat – No waiting for turns here. Watch the timeline of upcoming actions and bend it to your will. Stun enemies, speed up allies, and outthink the battlefield.

10 Unique Heroes (and counting) – Tanks, healers, glass-cannon DPS, sneaky debuffers — each with their own role and skills to master.

Relics & Gear – Equip game-changing relics for passive bonuses, or find powerful weapons and armor to customize your heroes mid-run.

Asynchronous PvP – Conquer PvE mode to register your victorious squad online. Challenge other victorious players in the Tower of Legends, climb the ladder, and prove your team reigns supreme.

Why You’ll Love It

If you enjoy games like Slay the Spire, Darkest Dungeon, or Into the Breach but wish you could mix their deep tactics with a little more pace and unpredictability, Mini Scouts is your next obsession. summary:
Lexomancer blends the satisfaction of word games with the tension of turn-based combat, wrapped in a stylized fantasy world where language itself is the ultimate magic.

Lexomancer is a word-based puzzle battle game where spells are cast by forming words; in this world, words have power.

You play a young arcanist who fights strange creatures born from fragments of a shattered magical lexicon. Each battle challenges you to build high-scoring words from a grid of letters, then unleash them as spells to defeat your enemies. Longer, rarer, or more clever words hit harder — but choosing the right kind of word matters just as much as raw score.

Enemies have strengths, weaknesses, and attack patterns of their own, pushing you to think strategically about which words you use, not just how many points they’re worth.

Word-Driven Combat

Form words from a grid of letters to cast spells. Damage is based on classic word-game scoring, enhanced by elemental affinities like Fire, Ice, Nature, and Arcane.

Strategic Enemies

Opponents don’t spell words themselves — instead, they use distinct move sets and behaviors. Learning their patterns and exploiting their vulnerabilities is key to survival.

Elemental Word Types

Certain enemies resist or take extra damage from specific kinds of words. A fiery creature might shrug off heat-related terms, but crumble when struck by cold or water-themed language.

Choose Your Path

Progress through themed “chapters” of a magical book, each focused on different elements and ideas. Zones can be tackled in different orders, and your choices subtly shape the challenges ahead — even in the final battle.

Grow Your Lexomancy

Unlock abilities that enhance specific word types or play styles. Specialize in arcane terms, favor short aggressive words, or master long, powerful vocabulary.

Designed for Replayability

With multiple playable characters, branching progression, and varied enemy encounters, no two runs play exactly the same.

Buy various squares from the shop, discover new synergies, and watch them bounce around the screen while they generate points. You only have 30 seconds per round. How far can you go?

In Naemo, you control a growing collection of bouncing squares. Each square behaves in its own way, and it’s up to you to figure out how they all work together.

Some squares generate points whenever they move or bounce, acting as the main way to push your score higher. Some squares provide buffs to other squares, making them stronger, faster, or more efficient. Others are triggered in different ways. Some every few seconds, some every time they hit a wall, and some only under special conditions. Watching them all move and interact creates a constant stream of chain reactions that can quickly fill the screen with energy.

Certain squares even reward clever pairings. For example, filling your stage with small-sized squares makes The Connoisseur shine, a unique square that only generates large bursts of points when it collides with smaller ones. Another option is The Axe, which delivers a high point payout whenever it collides with another square, but reduces the size of that square in the process. Pair it with squares that can regrow their size, and you’ll have a powerful cycle that keeps the points flowing. Discovering and experimenting with these synergies is the key to success.

Between rounds, you’ll have the chance to expand your setup. Spend your earnings in the shop to purchase new types of squares, upgrade your existing ones, or reroll for a better selection. Careful planning and experimentation are key, as sometimes a single well-timed synergy can carry you through an entire stage, while other times you’ll need to mix and match strategies to adapt.

summary:
A romantic loop 3D visual novel about a girl who forgets you every night. It’s always your first date. She resets. You don’t. Try to win her heart, or choose to let go. Another strange post from the town of Akabako.

? About This Game
There’s a girl at the ramen shop.
She looks up when you sit beside her, curious, kind, maybe a little distant.
You talk. You connect.
Then the next night, she doesn’t recognize you at all.

Welcome to It's You Again | また、きみだ。
A romance comedy (but ofc wholesome) about remembering someone who forgets.

You’re not here to fix her.
You’re here to find out if this feeling is real.

Will you try again?
Will she fall for you?
Or will you walk away?

This game is based on a post from the Akabako Community Message Board.
Username: soupagain.
Title: “She never remembers. But I can’t forget her.”

More soon.

Kōbako

? Gameplay Features

Talk to Her
You meet her at the ramen shop. She doesn’t remember.
You decide what kind of stranger you’ll be tonight.

Narrator Conflict
There’s a voice in your head.
It remembers everything.
You can listen to it… or fight back.

Multiple Outcomes
You can try to win her heart ?
Or you can let her go?

8 Possible Versions of Her 
If you ever decide to start over, really start over, you might meet someone a little different.
There are 8 possible versions of her, each with their own way of speaking, feeling, and connecting; The Child-Loving Illustrator. The Hopeless Romantic Kindergarten Teacher. The Free Spirited Model. The Sweet Baker. The Awkward Screenwriter. The Dreamy Ex-Figure Skater.... and more! 
She always forgets.
But maybe that’s the point.

? Universe Note
Part of the Kōbako Games
Short games. Long shadows.
Each Kōbako title is based on a thread from the Akabako Community Message Board: weird stories, ghost sightings, strangers, rumors, unfinished conversations. 

Some usernames repeat. Some stories connect.

The more you play, the more Akabako remembers you.

Mark Twain) has a dream: to build a riverboat that will rival the most magnificent paddle-wheelers ever navigated on the mighty Mississippi. Then, to steer it up the endless waterway that dominates his new home planet--and at last discover its hidden source.

But before he can carry out his plan, he first must undertake a dangerous voyage to unearth a fallen meteor. This mission would require striking an uneasy alliance with the bloodthirsty Viking Erik Bloodaxe, treacherous King John of England, legendary French swordsman Cyrano de Bergerac, Greek adventurer Odysseus, and the infamous Nazi Hermann Göring. All for the purpose of storming the ominous stone tower at the mouth of the river, where the all-powerful overseers of Riverworld--and their secrets--lie in wait..

summary:

But if that is the case, what is his real world like, and what is he actually doing every day when he thinks he is guessing 'Where Will the Little Green Man Be Next?'

summary:
All those who ever lived on Earth have found themselves resurrected--healthy, young, and naked as newborns--on the grassy banks of a mighty river, in a world unknown. Miraculously provided with food, but with no clues to the meaning of their strange new afterlife, billions of people from every period of Earth's history--and prehistory--must start again.

Sir Francis Bacon would be the first to glimpse the incredible way-station, a link between worlds. This forbidden sight would spur the renowned 19th-century explorer to uncover the truth. Along with a remarkable group of compatriots, including Alice Liddell Hargreaves (the Victorian girl who was the inspiration for Alice in Wonderland), an English-speaking Neanderthal, a WWII Holocaust survivor, and a wise extraterrestrial, Burton sets sail on the magnificent river. His mission: to confront humankind's mysterious benefactors, and learn the true purpose--innocent or evil--of the Riverworld...

Miraculously provided with food, but with no clues to the meaning of their strange new afterlife, billions of people from every period of Earth's history--and prehistory--must start again.

Sir Francis Bacon would be the first to glimpse the incredible way-station, a link between worlds. This forbidden sight would spur the renowned 19th-century explorer to uncover the truth. Along with a remarkable group of compatriots, including Alice Liddell Hargreaves (the Victorian girl who was the inspiration for Alice in Wonderland), an English-speaking Neanderthal, a WWII Holocaust survivor, and a wise extraterrestrial, Burton sets sail on the magnificent river. His mission: to confront humankind's mysterious benefactors, and learn the true purpose--innocent or evil--of the Riverworld...

name: Eye in the Sky
summary:
While sightseeing at the Belmont Bevatron, Jack Hamilton, along with seven others, is caught in a lab accident. When he regains consciousness, he is in a fantasy world of Old Testament morality gone awry—a place of instant plagues, immediate damnations, and death to all perceived infidels. Hamilton figures out how he and his compatriots can escape this world and return to their own, but first they must pass through three other vividly fantastical worlds, each more perilous and hilarious than the one before.

Winner of both the Hugo and John W. Campbell awards for best novel, widely regarded as the premiere science fiction writer of his day, and the object of cult-like adoration from his legions of fans, Philip K. Dick has come to be seen in a literary light that defies classification in much the same way as Borges and Calvino. With breathtaking insight, he utilizes vividly unfamiliar worlds to evoke the hauntingly and hilariously familiar in our society and ourselves.

name: 酔うと記憶をなくしちゃう後輩と飲み歩いた日々
summary:
漫画サークルの高嶺の花、容姿端麗な後輩女子・小崎海咲。
実は彼女は、お酒を飲むと豹変し記憶をなくすタイプだった！
ひょんなことから夜な夜な一緒に飲み歩き、海咲が仕掛ける過激な誘惑。
シラフだと純真、酔うと小悪魔な彼女に、俺の理性は限界寸前！
海咲の彼氏への罪悪感に苛まれつつ秘密の関係を深めるが、
やがて彼女の隠された本当の想いが明らかになって……
Ｗｅｂの人気小説に大幅加筆、最高に胸が熱くなる純愛青春ストーリー！

name: The Dark Design
summary:
Years have passed on Riverworld. Entire nations have risen, and savage wars have been fought--all since the dead of Earth found themselves resurrected in their magnificent new homeworld. Yet the truth about the Ethicals, the powerful engineers of this mysterious "afterlife," remains unknown. But a curious cross-section of humanity is determined to change that situation... at any cost.

Intrepid explorer Sir Richard Francis Burton leads the most remarkable voyage of discovery he has ever undertaken. Hot on his heels are Samuel Clemens, King John of England, and Cyrano de Bergerac. Spurred by the promise of ultimate answers, they chart a course across the vast polar sea--and toward the awesome tower that looms above it. But getting there will be more than half the battle. For death on Riverworld has become chillingly final...

name: Gods of Riverworld
summary:
Thirty-five billion people from throughout Earth's history were resurrected along the great and winding waterways of Riverworld. Most began life anew--accepting without question the sustenance provided by their mysterious benefactors. But a rebellious handful burned to confront the unseen masters who controlled their fate--and these few launched an invasion that would ultimately yield the mind-boggling truth.

Now Riverworld's omnipotent leaders have been confronted, and the renegades of Riverworld--led by the intrepid Sir Richard Francis Burton--control the fantastic mechanism that once ruled them. But the most awesome challenge lies ahead. For in the vast corridors and secret rooms of the tower stronghold, an unknown enemy watches and waits to usurp the usurpers...

name: The Game-Players of Titan
summary:
In this sardonically funny gem of speculative fiction, Philip K. Dick creates a novel that manages to be simultaneously unpredictable and perversely logical.
Poor Pete Garden has just lost Berkeley. He's also lost his wife, but he'll get a new one as soon as he rolls a three. It's all part of the rules of Bluff, the game that's become a blinding obsession for the last inhabitants of the planet Earth. But the rules are about to change--drastically and terminally--because Pete Garden will be playing his next game against an opponent who isn't even human, for stakes that are a lot higher than Berkeley.

summary:
A realistic bridge and COLREGs simulator built by an active-duty Navy officer for junior officers and maritime learners. Practice watchstanding, radar navigation, and CO trust management offline in Early Access.

Help Shape Watchstander

I built Watchstander because I wanted a way to practice real bridge watchstanding without needing a ship, a full bridge team, or an expensive simulator.

This isn’t combat — it’s about the reality of a watch: managing contacts, applying COLREGs, and earning the CO’s trust one decision at a time.

If you’ve ever stared down a radar contact, prepped for a Rules of the Road exam, or just wanted to keep your instincts sharp underway, this is for you.

Early Access is your chance to help shape it. Every bit of feedback matters. Buying now gets you every update, including the full 1.0 release, at no extra cost.

— A fellow watchstander

About the Game

Watchstander is a bridge watchstanding and COLREGs simulator built by an active-duty Navy officer to give junior officers, SWOs, and maritime learners a way to practice navigation and radar contact management offline.

This isn’t a combat game. It’s about the day-to-day reality of standing a watch: issuing helm and engine orders, evaluating risk of collision, tracking contacts, and earning the Captain’s trust one maneuver at a time.

I’m developing this solo alongside active service because I wanted a way to practice underway without needing a $500,000 bridge sim or a full watch team. Early Access lets me get this into the hands of other watchstanders early so we can shape it together.

Whether you’re preparing for a qualification board, studying COLREGs, or just want to keep your instincts sharp, I’d be grateful for your feedback as Watchstander evolves.

? Key Features (Early Access)

? Bridge Watch Mode – Simulate realistic watchstanding conditions including contact tracking, risk evaluation, and safe ship navigation.

⚓ Rules of the Road Practice – Apply COLREGs through realistic light
