BEARS!?

The island where the salmon are trying to climb upstream is home to an incredibly diverse number of "bears". While not belonging to the ursus (true bears) genus, the bear creatures on the island do currently belong to the ursidae (bears family), much like how the panda bear is not included amongst ursus genus, but rather the ailuropoda genus. However, much like the red panda losing its status as a "bear", zoologists may someday reclassify these bear-like creatures under different carnivore families.

...

JUMP AWAY FROM THE BEARS! They are ravenous for succulent salmon!

There's no better way to spend a beautiful autumn day than to crank up the old leaf blower and give a lawn the care it deserves. Or a winter day. Or a spring day. Or a stormy night.  Leaf Blower Something lets you experience the sheer joy of blasting leaves across a yard any time, any season, any weather.

Play as seasoned pro Juan or weekend warrior Ron. Blow the leaves into the designated area before time runs out. Get paid based on how many leaves make it into the pile — then use your earnings to upgrade your blower and keep it fueled up. Do poorly and you'll find yourself out of a job.

But don't get too comfortable. Each round, the challenge ramps up:

? The leaf spawn area grows — and the target pile shrinks.

?️ Animals show up and they are NOT here to help.

?️ Wind gusts get more frequent and more obnoxious.

? Obstacles show up more frequently.

⚠️ Random encounters keep things unpredictable.

Your leaf blower can be upgraded up to Level 5 for maximum power and fuel efficiency — but neglect it and it'll degrade on you mid-job. Keep it maintained, or suffer the consequences.

Rounds can be set to 15, 30, 45, or 60 seconds.  Each round length has its own settings and feel.

Not in the mood for chaos? Jump into the relaxed mode — no animals, no encounters, just you, your blower, and a yard full of leaves.

No inventory management. No perk cards. No 40-hour tutorial. Just pick up and play.

As Juan says, "Blowing es la vida." Exactamente, Juan. Exactamente.

summary:
The Manifesto Of Weeping (a minimalist emotional clicker) “Just click. Keep clicking. And in the end, it won’t be numbers that flow, it will be you.”

Press to Cry is a minimalist emotional clicker.

You want to put your life in order, but don’t know how.

Perhaps you’re not meant to fix anything at all.

You only need to click.

Each click increases a number on the screen.
That’s it.

There are no objectives to chase,
no scores to beat,
no failure states.

As the number grows, the experience slowly changes in tone and atmosphere.
The meaning you attach to the numbers is personal — the game does not tell you what to feel.

Some players see numbers as milestones.
Others see them as memories.
Some see nothing at all.

The game does not interpret the clicks for you.

It simply lets you continue.

At a certain point, the counter stops progressing visually.
But you can keep clicking.

Because by then, the action is no longer about the number.

It’s about the motion.

This is not a traditional game.
It is a quiet interaction.

A pause.
A loop.
A moment to sit with yourself.

?️ Gameplay

Single-button interaction (mouse click)

A rising counter with subtle audiovisual feedback

Minimalist presentation

No win or lose conditions

Designed to be experienced, not completed

Graverobber is a digger game about opening graves for profit while avoiding patrolling guards, traps, and whatever might be buried beneath the soil.

Graverobber is a first-person stealth game about digging graves at night while avoiding patrols, traps, and unwanted attention. Every grave is a decision: dig deeper for better rewards, or stop before someone notices.

You are not a hero. You are not a fighter. You are someone working quietly in the dark, reading the environment and deciding how much risk you’re willing to take.

Guards patrol the grounds with headlamps, sweeping narrow cones of light across the cemetery. Sound, movement, and timing matter. Staying hidden means watching patrol routes, working quickly, and knowing when to freeze.

Your dog is your early warning system. It does not bark or draw attention. When danger is near, it silently lies down, giving you a moment to react—if you’re paying attention.

Graves vary in depth, value, and danger. Some contain nothing. Some are trapped. Some hold more than you expected. Better tools let you dig faster and deeper, but rushing always carries risk.

Graverobber focuses on grounded tension rather than jump scares—quiet moments, subtle signals, and the constant feeling that you might be caught if you push your luck.

Key Features

First-person stealth gameplay focused on tension and awareness

Nighttime grave digging with risk-versus-reward decisions

Patrolling guards

Tools and upgrades that change how you approach each dig

Traps, surprises, and unpredictable outcomes beneath the soil

summary:
Soil is a slow-paced space RTS game where you mine resources, build ships and fight your enemies. Campaign features persistent fleet, research, and optional mission objectives that can affect rest of the missions.

Game features simulated projectiles, beams and missiles, and armor system that promotes variety of ships in your fleet.

Ships

Ships are composed of subsystems, which provide functions like engines, sensors, shipyards, fighterbays etc., and hardpoints that house turrets. Damaging them reduces their effectiveness, destroying them removes their function, or removes the turrets. Destroy the engines to prevent ship from moving, destroy reactor to strip ship of most of its energy generation, destroy fighterbay to prevent new fighters from being produced. Destroy hardpoint to remove its turrets from action. This type of damage can only be fixed by ships with shipyards for resources.

Ships in Soil gain two types of experience. Offensive experience is gained by causing damage and it increases ship's accuracy, rate of fire and other attributes. Defensive experience is gained by taking damage, and increases passive self-repair, and reduces incoming damage.

Fighters

Fighterbays on ships produce and house fighter or interceptor groups that can provide fighter cover, or bomber groups to supplement your firepower or perform precision strikes. Fighters need resources to be present on carrier to be built or repaired, and will also run out of ammo and fuel and will need to return to carrier to replenish those.

Resources & research

Soil has a single resource type for building ships and fighters. It is mined from asteroids or dropped cargo containers from exploding ships, and needs to be returned to the ship that will be using them. There is no global pool

summary:
Dillingham is a fast-paced fish-processing and logistics simulator where chaos meets precision. Run an Alaskan seafood plant, unload boats, sort and process fish, manage conveyor systems, operate forklifts, and keep every station flowing before the whole line backs up.

Dillingham is a deeply detailed fish-processing and factory-management game inspired by the real-world fast pace, pressure, and gritty charm of Alaskan seafood plants. You control a fully simulated facility where every station—from the pinner to the slimer to the deheader and freezer racks—plays a role in the chain of production. Boats arrive off-screen to unload fresh fish onto the dock, conveyors move product through machines with physics-driven behavior, AI workers operate based on class-specific rules, and forklifts shuttle boxes and racks to where they’re needed most. Every item has weight, state, type, z-height, and machine interactions, turning the plant into a living system you must constantly tune.

Whether you’re routing frozen racks, keeping belts from clogging, optimizing worker flow, or dealing with the unpredictable messiness of machinery jams, Dillingham pushes you to think strategically under pressure. With its blend of Overcooked-style action, factory-sim depth, and your signature procedural GameMaker engineering, it offers a uniquely immersive and satisfying take on industrial chaos. From dock to freezer, every moment is about staying sharp, staying fast, and keeping the line alive.

As you carry out your rituals, distant chanting rises through the trees. The tasks become heavier, stranger, more demanding—yet disobedience is not an option.

YOU DO NOT CONTROL THE HERO. YOU CONTROL THE UNIVERSE.

Welcome to Chronomaze: Gravity Maze, a study in minimalist precision where the only thing you can influence is the laws of physics themselves.

In most games, you move the character. Here, the character is helpless—a particle at the mercy of momentum. Your only tool is gravity. Change its direction to navigate tight corridors, build lethal velocity, and solve intricate physics puzzles before the clock runs out.
THE EXPERIENCE
Chronomaze is not about luck; it is about flow.

 Clinical Aesthetics: A high-contrast "Glow" visual style designed for pure clarity. No visual noise. Just the maze and the goal.

 Immersive Soundscape: A hypnotic soundtrack and responsive sound design built to keep you in the "zone."

 Respect for Your Time: No loading screens, no ads, no bloat.Pure focus.

CONTROLS
Simple to learn. Difficult to master.

 Arrow Keys: Shift Gravity (Up, Down, Left, Right)

DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
"The concept is simple. The execution is everything."

Chronomaze is the debut release from Gift Bytes Productions.
We built this game as a reaction against modern gaming bloat. We stripped away the microtransactions, the daily logins, and the noise to leave only what matters: A clean, honest, and challenging physics experience.

Whether you have 5 minutes or an hour, the maze is waiting.

summary:
When Grace Harland vanishes at Stillwater Lake, the police rule it an accident. Suspecting a cover-up, you venture into the dark, fog-choked waters alone. But as you piece together her final hours, you realise a local cult will do anything to keep the truth buried.

In this episode, you slip onto the restricted waters of Stillwater Lake, carrying out a dangerous favour for a friend to find Grace. What starts as a covert rescue mission rapidly descends into a nightmare of unsettling encounters. As your boat cuts through the dark open water, you begin to suspect that the local park rangers are covering up a terrifying secret.

Gameplay

Untold Cases: Stillwater Lake is the first episode of a first-person psychological horror anthology series.

The experience is a narrative-driven mystery focused on immersion and the feeling of being watched. You will use your radio to communicate with others and your boat to reach abandoned locations around the lake. With no HUD to break your immersion, you are forced to rely entirely on your instincts, your surroundings, and the haunting sounds of the water echoing in the dark.

Features

Episodic Horror: Experience a tightly paced, self-contained nightmare focused on heavy atmosphere, environmental storytelling, and creeping dread.

Manual Boat Navigation: Take physical control of your boat to traverse the oppressive, open waters of the lake as you travel between isolated docks and abandoned lakeside locations.

Radio Interaction: You are entirely alone, save for your handheld radio. Communicate with the mainland to piece together clues, unravel the mystery, and progress the story.

Psychological Dread: A slow-burn horror experience designed to get under your skin, prioritising thick tension and paranoia over cheap jump scares.

Local Conspiracy: Dig into the dark history of Stillwater Lake and uncover the terrifying truth behind a rumoured local cult and its ties to the authorities.

Power, control, and corruption shape every decision. After one impulsive mistake, Laura becomes entangled with a man who can erase problems — but every choice pulls her deeper.

ABOUT THE STORY

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

One impulsive mistake changes everything. What starts as a private incident quickly becomes leverage in someone else’s hands.

The only person who offers help is an influential associate of the mayor. He offers to fix things. The cost just isn’t visible at first.

It sounds simple. It never is.

Every favour comes with weight. Every solution creates dependency. And every step pulls her deeper. Soon, anonymous warnings begin to surface. Questions appear — without answers.

Laura is introduced to PAM — a company that needs a public face. She accepts because it feels like the safest option. At first, it looks like a professional opportunity.

But expectations begin to shift. Requests become patterns. Patterns become obligations. And her public image becomes harder to separate from the organisation behind it.

Outside of work, pressure builds. Her marriage begins to crack. Trust starts to erode. And control becomes harder to define.

Your choices determine how Laura responds.

Through the Pure / Corrupt psychological system, decisions shape her perception, unlock different scenes, and influence which relationships — and which truths — become available.

Each chapter tells its own part of the story — but your choices persist across the entire four-part narrative.

Chapter 1 sets the foundation. The consequences come later.

The invitation is only the beginning.

summary:
A narrative RPG of three intertwined stories, hidden secrets, and a broken timeline only the player can repair. Every ending reveals new paths, if you know where to look.

Welcome to The Village, a peaceful place where everything seems to unfold exactly as it should, at least at first glance. 
But this isn’t the story of a village. It’s the story of three paths, three lives that begin in the same place… and end far too soon.

Follow each protagonist as they try to move forward in their own journey. Every choice reveals something new, every deviation opens an unexpected possibility. Sometimes things stop abruptly. Sometimes they end badly.
And it’s in those endings that you begin to understand how this world truly works.

Each of the three characters brings a distinct playstyle, with unique ways of interacting with the world, solving situations, and advancing their storyline. Their perspectives don’t just differ narratively  they reshape how you approach the game itself.

But no character can progress on their own.
The story can only move forward through external knowledge, information learned from another protagonist’s path. By understanding what the others have seen, discovered, or failed to do, each character unlocks new possibilities and overcomes the limits of their own perspective. 
You are the only one who can bridge these gaps.

Survive the night shift at an abandoned school. Complete your cleaning tasks before 5 AM, manage your flashlight battery, and avoid the darkness that hunts you. Can you last 5 nights?

A Job You Can't Refuse

Joe was desperate. After countless rejections, he finally got a job offer a janitor at an old school. No interview. No questions. Just a Sunday start time and an address.

He arrived at 5 PM. The doors locked behind him. He woke up in a shed at midnight with a phone call explaining the rules. Complete your tasks. Survive until 5 AM. Return to the shed. Do this for 5 nights.

What waits in the darkness doesn't care about your resume.

Core Gameplay

Work the Night Shift

- Complete cleaning tasks around the school: mop floors, clean spills, wipe windows, repair broken desks

- Manage your limited tool inventory (carry 3 tools at a time)

- Return to the safe house (janitor's shed) before 5:00 AM

Survive the Dark Zone

- A roaming darkness patrols the school hallways

- Your flashlight is your only defense it pushes the darkness away

- Stay too long in the dark and you won't survive

- The Dark Zone grows stronger each week

Manage Your Resources

- Flashlight battery drains over time find batteries to recharge

- Collect fuses to restore power to dark areas

- Use the vending machine for energy drinks

Three-Week Structure

Week 1 - Joe's Story

Learn the rules. Complete your tasks. Survive. Notes scattered around the school hint at what happened to those who came before you.

Week 2 - The Detective

Someone else is trapped now. They're investigating the disappearances. They find Joe's notes. His handwriting gets worse each day.

Week 3 - The Origin

How did this all begin? Play as the first person to discover the truth about this place.

5 nights per week. Difficulty escalates each night.

Features

Environmental Storytelling

- Discover notes left by previous victims

- Piece together the mystery of the abandoned school

- Each week reveals a different persp

One Day To Live is a post-apocalyptic VR zombie survival game where every sunrise could be your last. 

The Outbreak

What began as a controllable virus spiraled into apocalypse when the vaccine's efficacy diminished. Governments collapsed, cities fell silent, and billions succumbed. Now, scattered survivors like you scavenge the remnants of civilization, racing against the clock to secure your next injection. The infected, once friends, family, and strangers, roam in relentless packs, their humanity lost to the insatiable hunger. Will you outlast the dawn, or become one of them?

Core Gameplay Features

Time-Critical Survival: Your life hangs on a 24-hour cycle. Track your infection levels in real-time as they increase, forcing desperate decisions. Raid a fortified military facility for boosters, or risk a detour through zombie-infested homes? Every choice impacts your fate.

Open World: Explore a vast wasteland spanning abandoned neighborhoods, overgrown forests, industrial ruins, and hidden bunkers. Weather events, day-night cycles, and evolving zombie behaviors keep the environment unpredictable and deadly.

Resource Management: Scavenge for medical supplies, weapons, and boosters. 

Intense Combat and Stealth: Face hordes with improvised tactics or clever distractions. Go loud with explosions and full-auto, or slip through shadows to avoid detection. Mutated zombie variants add layers of horror, from fast-runners to armored brutes.

Permadeath and Replayability: Death is permanent, but each run unlocks new starting locations and world variations. Difficulty levels amp up the tension with shorter infection windows, fewer items, and super tough zombies.

Multiplayer CO-OP or Free-For-All: Play with friends, or enemies...

summary:
Samota is a Solitaire roguelike deckbuilder. You don't draw cards but instead arrange a pile of cards so it will create huge synergy. Find a bunch of unique effects, buffs, modifiers, relics and uncover the secret this game hides! All of it so that the number goes big and bigger!

Samota is a Solitaire roguelike deckbuilder focused on strategic decision making. You have only one try per round and no draw to surpass the goal score. You must decide how to arrange your stacks, when to play or hold your cards, and which effects to combine to create powerful synergies.

Basic cards (Ace through King) have no innate effects; instead, you must combine them with Special Cards. Some effects favor low numbered cards or face cards, while others reward descending order stacks. You can even choose not to combine them, using cards to prolong a stack and break the traditional 13 card limit. Create game breaking synergies to win and uncover hidden cards, covers, and decks.

Secrets are found both inside and outside of your runs. Discover secret codes to unlock hidden rounds that offer difficult trials. Should you pass, you will be bestowed with a powerful Cover to accompany you!

Utilize a variety of tools that require careful consideration: Covers, Zodiacs, Minor Arcana, Virtues, and Callspot modifiers. These tools appear rarely, so every decision is meaningful.

100 Special Cards: Use these to enhance your cards or prolong stacks beyond the 13 card limit.

50 Covers: Each provides a unique effect that impacts the entire board.

12 Zodiacs: Modifiers that provide rewards for not using certain cards.

4 Minor Arcana: Level up your cards based on the number of colored cards you possess.

6 Callspot Modifiers: Grant unique effects to specific stacks, ensuring no two stacks are ever the same.

10 Decks: Each featuring different modifiers.

10 Challenges per deck.

5 Secret Rounds to earn powerful Covers.

name: Veniss Underground
summary:
In his debut novel, literary alchemist Jeff VanderMeer takes us on an unforgettable journey, a triumph of the imagination that reveals the magical and mysterious city of Veniss through three intertwined voices. First, Nicholas, a would-be Living Artist, seeks to escape his demons in the shadowy underground–but in doing so makes a deal with the devil himself. In her fevered search for him, his twin sister, Nicola, spins her own unusual and hypnotic tale as she discovers the hidden secrets of the city. And finally, haunted by Nicola's sudden, mysterious disappearance and gripped by despair, Shadrach, Nicola's lover, embarks on a mythic journey to the nightmarish levels deep beneath the surface of the city to bring his love back to light. There he will find wonders beyond imagining…and horrors greater than the heart can bear.

By turns beautiful, horrifying, delicate, and powerful, Veniss Underground explores the limits of love, memory, and obsession in a landscape that defies the boundaries of the imagination. This special edition includes the short stories "The Sea, Mendeho, and Moonlight"; "Detectives and Cadavers"; and "A Heart for Lucretia" and the novella Balzac's War, offering a complete tour of the fantastic world of Veniss.

name: Shriek: An Afterword
summary: Narrated with flamboyant intensity by one-time society figure Janice Shriek, and presenting a vivid gallery of strange characters and even stranger events, this is an account of the adventures of her brother Duncan, a historian obsessed with a doomed love affair and a dark secret that may kill or transform him. It involves, too, a war between rival publishing houses which threatens to change Ambergris forever, and rivalry with a marginalised race known as the "grey caps" who, armed with advanced fungal technologies, wait underground for their chance to recover the city that was once theirs. This story of the family Shriek is an exotic and colourful novel of love, life and death which brings to fruition the author's genius for capturing the truly weird.

name: Finch
summary:
In Finch, mysterious underground inhabitants known as the gray caps have reconquered the failed fantasy state Ambergris and put it under martial law. They have disbanded House Hoegbotton and are controlling the human inhabitants with strange addictive drugs, internment in camps, and random acts of terror. The rebel resistance is scattered, and the gray caps are using human labor to build two strange towers.

Against this backdrop, John Finch, who lives alone with a cat and a lizard, must solve an impossible double murder for his gray cap masters while trying to make contact with the rebels. Nothing is as it seems as Finch and his disintegrating partner Wyte negotiate their way through a landscape of spies, rebels, and deception. Trapped by his job and the city, Finch is about to come face to face with a series of mysteries that will change him and Ambergris forever.

name: Borne
summary:
The Strange Bird is a new kind of creature, built in a laboratory -- she is part bird, part human, part many other things. But now the lab in which she was created is under siege and the scientists have turned on their animal creations. Flying through tunnels, dodging bullets, and changing her colors and patterning to avoid capture, the Strange Bird manages to escape.

But she cannot just soar in peace above the earth. The sky itself is full of wildlife that rejects her as one of their own, and also full of technology -- satellites and drones and other detritus of the human civilization below that has all but destroyed itself. And the farther she flies, the deeper she finds herself in the orbit of the Company, a collapsed biotech firm that has populated the world with experiments both failed and successful that have outlived the corporation itself: a pack of networked foxes, a giant predatory bear. But of the many creatures she encounters with whom she bears some kind of kinship, it is the humans -- all of them now simply scrambling to survive -- who are the most insidious, who still see her as simply something to possess, to capture, to trade, to exploit. Never to understand, never to welcome home.

name: Red Planet
summary: A young colonist on Mars befriends a strange round creature called Willis who gets him into trouble when he goes away to school, but whose presence and friendship finally enable the colonials to negotiate a treaty with the Martians.

《陆海之战》于2025年12月7日在BBC One首播，连播前两集，并计划于2026年在Disney+上线。该剧获得评论界的普遍好评，尤其称赞演员的表演（特别是雷德格雷夫的演绎）以及剧集与《火炬木小组》的相似之处。

Everything on Black! Build a balanced deck of fighters - or double down on specific outcomes.

Fighters multiply the winning number to block and attack - if their color matches the winning color. Each fighter also has a specific rule, for example "Extra attack if number < 5" or "Ignore enemy block".

A physics‑based sandbox 2D adventure of survival and exploration. Gather resources to build bases, contraptions, and outposts on land or in space, but since everything keeps its mass, hauling it around requires smart planning.

Playtest

I'm sharing the entire development journey and I'd love to get continous feedback to help development! (See the YouTube link in the sidebar)

Right click inside the "zone" to start building!

You can move, resize, combine, split, and delete shapes in there

Select two shapes in the zone, and then right click one, to see the "joint" menu

Current State

The game is very rough around the edges and even crashes sometimes (mostly when shapes are deleted by colliding too hard), so be warned, save often!

You can enable god mode with G, but that's only meant for testing purposes.

Press Esc -> Controls to see a list of all controls.

Survival Scenario

A randomized spawn on a planet with average gravity. Use your initial minimal resources to build a contraption to try and bring back a boulder to the station, increasing your resources. You can build and delete anything that's inside the "zone" (focus on one of the walls to activate it).

Venture east to find an abandoned miner, if you manage to bring power and storage then you can fire it up the get even more resources!

Once you've attained some rare resources you can construct more Zone Modules, letting you modify your zone! If you chose to expand your starter zone you'll need a contraption that can for example lift and torch your wall, to insert more segments by lifting and welding them together. But be careful! Unwelded zone modules do not create a zone, so ensure you've planned accordingly before starting construction!

The physics are generalized, you could slap a thruster on a planet for example, to change its orbit.

The game is rather unforgiving so be prepared to restart multiple times

Negative Time is a top-down shooter with bullet hell and roguelike elements where each time you get hit, you are sent further and further back in time, until you are sent into the past they tried so hard to erase. A past before time began - NEGATIVE TIME.

Get more powerful by collecting new weapons in this past realm. Then, when time becomes positive, use your newfound power to make it further through the halls of enemies in order to defeat the ones who erased you from existence.

Time Travel

Each time you die, you are sent back in time a number of seconds, called your interval. Then next time, your interval is double what it was previously. If your interval sends you back before the game started, you enter NEGATIVE TIME - an inverted copy of the game, with its own unique enemies, and new weapons to unlock.

Weird Weapons

Curate your loadout of unique weapons from 5 different tiers and 3 different categories. Some of these weapons are quite strange - try to find good combinations!

Blessings

Collect blessings to power up yourself and your weapons. But don't think you can just wait around and get by on god's gifts, because these boons don't last forever!

Difficult Opponents

Face off against 4 bosses and 20+ regular enemies, as you try to dodge their bouncing, exploding, predicting, homing, and wall-piercing bullets - even one hit sends you back before your mistake, so at the end of the day, you'll need to be flawless if you hope to win.

Momentum is your weapon. Thrust, charge, and slam your friends into the void in this fast-paced physics brawler for up to 4 players. Built for social mayhem and brutal competition, Thrust Me Bro is couch-multiplayer chaos that’s easy to learn and hard to master. Get ready to Thrust.

CONGRATULATIONS, YOU'RE A PROJECTILE NOW.

Other games give you weapons. We made YOU the weapon. Specifically, a round, angry, hurtling-through-space weapon who's about to ruin someone's whole trajectory.

Up to 4 human cannonballs per arena. Aim optional. Regret guaranteed.

CHARGE — Go faster.

SLAM — Introduce your friend to the concept of "uncontrolled trajectory."

Newton's laws don't care about your intentions. Neither do we.

INTRODUCING: HIGH-VELOCITY DISRESPECT.

Why thrust yourself when you can throw things at people?

We call it "The Friendship Ender." Your friends will call it "Dream Breaker."

summary:
Enter the tomb of the Pharaess and tactically maneuver through a plethora of challenges and monster-filled gauntlets in this homage to strategy roguelikes of the 90s.

Overture!

HIEROSAGA: OVERTURE is the initial proof-of-concept iteration of the game presenting the first chapter of the story. It covers the arrival into the desert town of Akimor and the majority of the first dungeon. It also includes an infinite mode that takes full advantage of the generation algorithm for a more roguelike experience!

What's going on?

HIEROSAGA chronicles the adventure of a small town knight who journeys to a mythical desert town in the east seeking riches and ancient treasure. Along the way, he crosses paths with a gang of rowdy slave traders, as well as their captive: a scheming mage who unknowingly manages to land all of them - and perhaps even the world - in hot water.

The DNA

HIEROSAGA is a rogue-lite tactical role playing adventure inspired by games like Azure Dreams, Tactics Ogre, and Chrono Trigger. Featuring a free movement "Exploration mode" when out of combat, discover secrets and collect helpful items at your own pace- unearth artefacts that grant you skills and play around with your build in the equip menu to prepare for whatever might be around the corner. A grid-based "Combat mode" is triggered when an enemy is nearby, affixing the player to the "battle board" and turning the dungeon into a turn-based chess match where the name of the game can be escape, survival, or elimination of all enemies!

summary:
The labyrinth is waiting for challengers! Free demo available. Enter a giant dark labyrinth with limited light, ammo, health, and time. Find the keys, survive traps and enemies, and escape within 60 minutes.

Can you escape this colossal maze within 60 minutes?

Lost in the Dark Labyrinth is a maze-exploration survival FPS set inside a colossal labyrinth built on a near world-largest scale.

With only a weak personal light and scattered braziers to guide you, you must navigate twisting corridors and looming chambers and find a way out before time runs out.

The maze is huge and deliberately complex.

Similar-looking junctions, sudden open spaces, and vertical shifts between floors make it almost impossible to grasp the full layout on your first attempt.

The more you challenge it, the more you slowly learn, map, and master the labyrinth in your head.

Sneak past threats… or fight for an advantage

Dangerous enemies roam the maze, and the tension spikes the moment you sense them nearby.

You can try to avoid them and slip past in the dark, or take the risk and engage.

Defeating enemies will sometimes cause keys, health items, or coins to drop, giving you a valuable edge in your escape — but only if you survive.

Doors, keys, and the path forward

The labyrinth features multiple door types and matching keys.

As you progress through the stages, new door–key pairs are introduced, and finding the key required in that stage becomes critical to pushing deeper into the maze.

If you fail to secure the necessary key, you simply will not reach the exit.

Step by step, run by run, you piece together your own personal route to freedom.

60 minutes of pressure and replay

This maze is not meant to be cleared on your first attempt.

Instead, each run teaches you a little more — a landmark you recognize, a safer corridor, a dead end to avoid next time.

The 60-minute time limit keeps every decision sharp, while the enormous scale and branching paths give the game strong replayab

summary:
Idle Jumper is a fast-paced platformer where your character jumps automatically, your job is to upgrade their abilities, and climb endlessly upward. Simple to start but deeply rewarding to optimize, Idle Jumper blends the addictive progression of an idle game with the feel of a endless jumper.

In Idle Jumper, you control a tiny slime who jumps forever—your task is to help them reach new heights by unlocking upgrades, managing momentum, collecting coins, and discovering new power-ups. Whether you prefer an active playstyle filled with strategizing each move, or a more relaxed idle approach while watching your character improve over time, Idle Jumper grows with the way you want to play.

As you progress, you’ll earn resources to invest in permanent upgrades, boost your jumping power, unlock new modifiers, and automate mechanics to increase your long-term efficiency. Each run becomes more powerful than the last, letting you soar past previous milestones and discover how high you can climb.

Key Features: 

• Addictive idle–platformer hybrid gameplay 

• Smooth jumping physics with momentum-based progression 

• Meaningful upgrade paths that evolve your character over time 

• Idle playstyle

• Permanent progression keeps every run rewarding 

• Relaxing visual style and easy-to-learn mechanics 

• Endless vertical climb with scaling challenges

Idle Jumper is designed to be fun in short sessions or long idle stretches—perfect for players who enjoy growth, experimentation, and the joy of watching numbers go up.

Sealed away in an ancient alternate dimension, you must find a way to break free. In this fantasy action roguelike, uncover a variety of spells to cast your way through waves of hostile magical apparitions. Discover the secrets of Avernoth to make escape possible. Do you have what it takes?

You Must Escape Avernoth!

After being sealed away during a fight with a powerful rival mage, Allister is sealed away in an ancient alternate dimension and stripped of his magical powers. Alone, with almost no magic power at his disposal, Allister is faced with the reality that he must escape from a world from which no person has escaped before.

Uncover a Variety of Spells and Upgrades!

Each time you attempt to escape Avernoth, you are given a set of spells and abilities that determine your style of play. Throughout each escape attempt, find and acquire upgrades to your spells and new abilities that further increase your chances at escaping. Craft your experience to make each run feel unique!

Uncover Secrets

Scattered throughout Avernoth are clues that reveal more about Avernoth’s origin as well as the way to escape. Collect clues and complete objectives to reveal answers lost to time!

Key Features

Fast-Paced Magic Combat: Cast spells in quick succession to create lengthy combos while battling enemies.

Randomized Playstyle: Each escape attempt features a different set of spells, abilities, and upgrades that the player encounters along their journey.

Overarching Progression: Complete objectives during escape attempts to get closer to the goal of escaping Avernoth.

summary:
This is a little 30-40 minute experience where you explore the safest space of all: Your home. Live a day solving little problems and wandering around your house. It's just you and your mind...

In this game, you'll live a happy and peaceful day in your home, exploring a variety of rooms and solving little household problems... or that was the initial plan. As the lights go off, your home stops feeling as safe as before, and the focus shifts to solving a single problem: surviving.

Run and hide. Those are the only tools at your disposal to protect yourself. The thing is... what do you even have to protect yourself from? It's only you in the house after all... and that might exactly be the problem. With nothing but your mind accompanying you, the fear won't take long to start playing tricks on you.

Do your best to survive in this walking-sim that aims to deliver a horror experience, and try not to be consumed by fear...

Key Features:

The game crafts a very atmospheric, plausible experience to intensify the horror.

The gameplay consists in walking. And a walking simulator is a perfect fit for what The Safe Space of Home aims to deliver. You can only walk or sprint to where the game wants you to go, and that vulnerability is the key to the experience.

Even with a simple gameplay, the game puts you through a variety of situations, with the house transforming on itself, making you feel like you don't know the place you should know the most.

summary:
A 2.5D action-adventure platformer set in a land of forgotten gods. Armed with a bayonet and bound to a goddess you can't trust, fight through a single connected world, learn the bosses the hard way, and take back the throne the gods above her stole.

Voltumna is an action-adventure platformer with deep exploration. You play a lone soldier back from the trenches, bound by a pact to a goddess he cannot trust. The world is one connected map of forgotten gods. Fight through it with a bayonet, the powers she grants you, and whatever gear you can pry off its rulers.

READ THE ATTACK, EARN THE STRIKE

Parry at the right moment and the opening is yours. Dodge through what you can't block. Mistime either and the bayonet won't save you.

EXPLORE THE WORLD, UNCOVER ITS SECRETS

A single connected map runs from sunlit countryside down into tombs that should have stayed sealed. Shortcuts open behind you as you grow stronger, and the world keeps hiding things you weren't ready to see.

EARN NEW ABILITIES, BECOME SOMETHING ELSE

New movement and combat abilities open paths you couldn't reach before. Weapons, armor, and skills shape the soldier you need to become. The further you go, the less you resemble the one who walked in.

FACE THE GODS, LEARN THEIR PATTERNS

Each boss is born from forgotten myth, with patterns that punish guesswork. Read them, survive them, and walk away with something they can't take back.

Dunjinn is a deliberate, turn-based crawl where every step advances enemies, so stealth, noise, and light control matter. Hazards appear dynamically, and no two runs feel exactly the same. You’ll need to pay attention, act quickly, and prioritize what matters most in the moment.

There’s no combat, no complex controls, and no overwhelming systems. Just a beach, a few hatchlings, and the responsibility of getting them to the ocean.

Two Ways to Play

Story Mode - Progress through levels that gradually ramp up in difficulty. The beach gets longer, the turtle moves faster, and the crabs become more aggressive. You only have one life per level so if a hatchling doesn’t make it, you’ll need to start again.

Survival Mode - Test your reflexes in an endless scrolling beach where the goal is to survive as long as possible and earn a high score. The longer you last, the harder things get, but clear enough hazards and you’ll unlock power-ups that help you survive just a little longer

summary:
A 90s CGI-inspired FPS where players battle each other in fast-paced matches combining unique weapons and abilities to synergize and outplay the competition.

Boot up. Insert Floppy Disk. Fight

Bryce Canyon is a 90s CGI-inspired online multiplayer FPS where 2-4 players battle it out in fast-paced rounds of chaos, strategy, and style. Set inside a computer straight out of the late 90s CGI software era, slot floppy disks into the drive to select your weapons and abilities, then drop straight into the fight.

How It Works

Every game, players are dealt a random hand of floppy disks and must choose one weapon and one ability before the round begins. The twist: easier weapons earn fewer points, while riskier, harder-to-use weapons reward bigger scores. Last player standing takes the points. Master the combos, read the map, and outplay your friends — or get wiped out in seconds by someone who drew a black hole gun.

Key Features

Fast-paced free-for-all matches — 2-4 players, one life per round, winner takes points

Card-based loadout system with risk/reward scoring that keeps every round unpredictable

A wild arsenal ranging from SMGs and AKs to fire bows and electric guns

Maps that reward different playstyles depending on your weapon draw

Authentic 90s Bryce CGI aesthetic with chunky characters, rendered environments, and drum and bass soundtrack

Play Test Access

Bryce Canyon is in active early development. The current build features free-for-all multiplayer with a core set of weapons, abilities, and maps. On the roadmap: more maps, expanded card pools, new game modes, and eventually a solo mode. Your feedback directly shapes what gets built next.

summary:
In A Little Physics Roguelike aim to grab the best equipment, then build your unique board with a variety of item to defeat cute enemies.

In this game inspired by pachinko and coin-pusher traditional games, aim carefully and throw your cute character to get the best equipment. Either for fighting your enemies or to collect resources. These little bouncy fellows can be clumsy and will require all your skill to take the right path and grab as many stuff as they can.

Your board is your deck. Build it, change it, improve it. Add layers and layers of weapons and money to equip your characters. They don't have hands so they can grab anything matching their color.

If infinite replayability is not enough ? Compare your performances on the worldwide leaderboard.
